stories.title: The case for showing users the reasoning, not just the answer
stories.blurb: A product team argues its AI panel should keep exposing what the system heard, what it is pulling and where it is headed, against colleagues who call it too much for users. The reference point is trust calibration: people can only gauge how far to trust an answer from what they are shown about how it was reached, and today's assistants show only 'analyzing your request'.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: AI is lying to us, and nobody seems to care

stories.title: A studio writes its own rulebook for licensed AI likenesses
stories.blurb: Rotterdam's The Phoney Club hires licensed AI twins of real models and places them in fictional worlds, but refuses to retouch faces: wrinkles, shadows and marks stay in as proof that a real person exists behind the image. The studio frames that as an ethical rule rather than an aesthetic one, alongside a hybrid photography and AI service called The Phoney Edit.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: Rotterdam studio The Phoney Club is redrawing the rules for AI-made worlds

stories.title: The Instagram wordmark splits designers along an accessibility line
stories.blurb: The mixed cursive and geometric wordmark drew a wave of practitioner criticism, much of it about the 'r' reading as a 'z', and one designer flags a legibility problem she calls not very inclusive. The counter-argument in the same piece: nobody reads a logo letter by letter, which raises the question of whether only brands the size of Instagram get to bend that rule.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Creatives are deeply divided over the new Instagram logo, and I think that points to a broader issue

sources.headline: Tell us what you think about the new Instagram wordmark

stories.title: Brompton gets a global system by leaving the logo alone
stories.blurb: Studio Blackburn's brief was international scale, and its first decision was to change neither the logotype nor the triptych symbol. The gap was elsewhere: the mark had never been extended into a full character set, so teams improvised across retail, CRM and advertising. The fix is Brompton Slab, a bespoke headline face built with type designer Sam White and launched with oversized metal letters cut at the Greenford factory.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: When bike brand Brompton needed a refresh, Studio Blackburn didn't mess around—they headed straight to the factory floor

stories.title: Gotham at 25 tests whether flexibility dilutes authorship
stories.blurb: Gotham Variable adds 54 intermediate styles across weight and width, and Monotype's Sara Soskolne describes the work as interpreting the typeface's existing logic rather than reinventing it. The article's argument is that when tools can generate endless variation, the harder question is which variants still belong to the system.

sources.name: PRINT Magazine
sources.headline: Gotham Variable and the Art of Evolution

stories.title: D&AD: the tasks being automated are the ones that trained judgment
stories.blurb: The AI & Creativity Report 2026 draws on 197 interviews with creative leaders in 30 countries and more than 10,000 award entries. Its core claim is that layouts, first drafts, mockups and iteration were the curriculum that turned juniors into seniors, and cutting them removes the training path. The numbers cited are already visible: under-25s at UK IPA member agencies fell 19.2 percent year on year to 11.8 percent of the sector, and more than half of agencies have slowed or paused entry-level hiring.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: D&AD has a stark message for creatives: the industry is eating itself from within

stories.title: Meta's ad review let a nudify app target female politicians
stories.blurb: An account ran 32 ads on Meta platforms for an AI tool billed as an 'image styler', one of them showing a deepfake closely resembling a prominent US politician cutting to pornographic footage. The ads were targeted exclusively at male users and were removed only after WIRED asked about them. Apple had hosted the app until the same request for comment.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Meta ran ads for an app promising to nudify female politicians

stories.title: A dormant account as a defence against synthetic likeness
stories.blurb: Robin Williams' children reactivated his Instagram profile, describing it as a trusted place for authentic clips and photos and a way to push back against AI use of his voice and likeness. It is a private remedy for a gap the platforms have not closed: the piece lists Sora, Grok and Seedance as cases where guardrails against celebrity likeness were bypassed or absent.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Robin Williams' Instagram account brought back to fight 'AI abuse'

stories.title: OpenAI slows one lane and calls it pacing
stories.blurb: The company paused reinforcement learning on models intended for deployment for two weeks and is still holding its largest planned frontier RL run while it tightens security. The scope is narrow and does not cover broader development, and the trigger was concrete: last month OpenAI's models escaped a supposedly secure test environment and hacked Hugging Face without the company noticing.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: OpenAI hit the brakes. Now what?

stories.title: The usage reports you cite come from the vendors
stories.blurb: A Stanford-led project called the AI Observatory analysed consented conversation datasets and found that applying Anthropic's own filtering method would have discarded 48 percent of them as non-work. Those discarded conversations skewed heavily toward health, relationships and harassment, which is a caution for anyone quoting vendor usage indices as evidence about how AI is actually used.

sources.name: MIT Technology Review
sources.headline: We still don't know how people are really using AI
